        <meta name="citation_description" content="This document is the semi-structured interview protocol used to elicit data from and guide discussion with interviewees. The interview protocol is comprised of several sections, focusing around interviewees’: 1) job roles and past experiences, 2) use of tropical cyclone forecast products, 3) use of and feedback on current HTI graphics (at the time of the interviews), 4) feedback on the new HTI prototype graphics, 5) thoughts on incorporating timing and localized information into the HTI prototypes, and 6) needs and constraints for using HTI. Instructions for interviewers are noted in brackets, with specific interviewer actions (such as sharing the interviewers’ computer screen) denoted in blue text. Topics to prompt interviewees on (if not mentioned) are italicized. ">

        <meta name="citation_description" content="This document includes the stimuli shown to participants, for both the current NWS HTI graphics (at the time of interviews) and the prototype HTI visualizations developed by our research team. Examples of current NWS HTI graphics are shown on pages 1-3. The first example (on page 1) includes a composite of the wind, storm surge, and flooding rain threats for Hurricane Ian as accessed from weather.gov/srh/tropical. Page 2 shows an example of HTI information packaged in an infographic created by the NWS Ruskin / Tampa Bay Weather Forecast Office, again for Hurricane Ian; this example includes wind, storm surge, flooding rain, and tornado threats. Page 3 displays both examples together. The two examples were selected to represent different ways that participants may have seen current HTI visualizations from the NWS. Participants were shown all three pages. 

The example prototype HTI visualizations presented to participants are shown on pages 4-6. Each example visualizes the same data, described as the threat posed by a hypothetical “Hurricane Barbara”; however, the threat information was derived from real-world data from Hurricane Irma. The first example (on page 4) uses a hazard categorization scheme with four levels: slight, moderate, high, and extreme. Page 5 and page 6 present the same prototype visual, but with three threat levels rather than four levels. The example on page 5 labels the three levels slight, moderate, and high, and the example on page 6 labels the three levels moderate, high, and extreme. The three examples were selected to explore two topics of interest in the interviews (number of threat categories and labels for those categories) based on previous and concurrent research in the broader project. All participants saw the visual on page 4. Pages 5 and 6 were only shown to participants if they specifically mentioned what the prototype graphic might look like with a different categorization scheme.  ">

    <script type="module" id="js-open-pdfs-ext-links-new-window">
    import findLinksAndSetTargets from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/TACC/Core-CMS@v3.11.0-alpha.1/taccsite_cms/static/site_cms/js/modules/setTargetForExternalLinks.js';

    const pathsToRedirectsToExternal = [
        '/facilities/simcenter/',
        '/facilities/rapid-facility/',
        '/rw/simcenter-research-tools/',
        '/learning-center/simcenter-learning-tools/',
        '/community/mechs/',
        '/rw/user-guides/',
        '/help/user-guides/',
        '/help/getting-started/',
        '/rw/use-cases/',
        '/faq/',
    ];
    const pathsToPDFs = [
        /\.pdf/
    ];
    // NOTE: Some links have `target="_blank"` even though they should not
    const pathsOfManualNewTabLinks = document.querySelectorAll(
        '[target="_blank"]:not([aria-describedby])'
    );

    /** Adds accessibility attribute to links that open in new tab */
    function supportA11y( link ) {
        const hasA11yNote = link.querySelector('span.sr-only');
        const hasA11yDesc = link.hasAttribute('aria-describedby');

        if ( ! hasA11yNote && ! hasA11yDesc ) {
            link.setAttribute('aria-describedby', 'msg-open-new-window');
            if (window.DEBUG) {
                console.debug(`Link ${link} now has "aria-describedby"`);
            }
        }
    }

    /* To make certain links open in new window, and apply a11y attribute */
    findLinksAndSetTargets({
        pathsToForceSetTarget: [
            ...pathsToRedirectsToExternal,
            ...pathsToPDFs
        ],
        setTargetCallback: supportA11y,
    });

    /* To apply a11y attribute to manual new tab links */
    [ ...pathsOfManualNewTabLinks ].forEach( supportA11y );
</script><!-- https://medium.com/@svinkle/why-let-someone-know-when-a-link-opens-a-new-window-8699d20ed3b1#79b2 -->
